extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, supervisory patent examiners (SPEs), Technology Center staff, Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) and reexamination clerks
extracted.subtask_description: Policies, procedural requirements, and adjudicative criteria for handling ex parte reexamination requests of patents (including assignment, reporting, transfer, timing, decision standards, and special situations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting events to PALM
rubrics_metrics.description: The PALM system is used to monitor major events that take place in processing reexamination proceedings. The TC reexamination clerk is responsible for reporting events using the reexamination icon/window in PALM EXPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events to be reported include: (1) Determination Mailed — Denial of request for reexamination; (2) Determination Mailed — Grant of request for reexamination; (3) Petition for reconsideration of determination received; (4) Decision on petition mailed — Denied; (5) Decision on petition mailed — Granted; (6) Owner response to determination (owner’s statement) received; (7) Requester response (requester’s reply) received; (8) The mailing of all examiner actions; (9) The receipt of owner’s responses to examiner’s actions and Office receipt date. Each reported event is permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM and reflected in status codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM status reports and ticklers
rubrics_metrics.description: Various weekly automated 'tickler' reports produced from PALM to ensure reexaminations are processed with special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified reports include: Requests Not Yet Received in TC; Requests Not Yet Assigned to an Examiner (highlight those not assigned by 6th week); Requests Which Should Be Taken Up for Determination (assigned but no determination mailed and past 6th week); Requests for Which Determinations Should be Prepared (no determination and past 2nd month); Requests for Which Determinations Should Have Been Mailed (no determination and past 10th week) — these and several 'Overdue' reports (Overdue Determinations — should always be zero; Overdue Petitions for Reconsideration; Overdue Owner Responses to Determinations; Overdue Requester Responses to Statements; Overdue First Ex Parte Actions; Overdue Action or Examiner’s Answer; Overdue Advisory Action; Overdue Owner Response; Overdue Certificates; Requests With Prolonged Prosecution). Items marked with an asterisk require immediate action and follow-up. Reports are subdivided by TC working group and list requests in control number sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner assignment policy for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination requests should normally be assigned to the art unit which examines the class/subclass in which the patent is currently classified; the SPE will assign the reexamination to a primary examiner other than the original examiner who examined the patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy: generally the SPE will assign to an examiner different from those previously involved in examining the patent (including conferees). Exceptions: (a) where the SPE is the only primary examiner in the art unit, or (b) where the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge of the relevant technology — in such cases TC Director approval is required and must be stated in the decision on the request. If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner may be assigned to the new reexamination. For copending reissue and reexamination proceedings follow the specified reassignment and merger rules (OPLA handles merger; merged proceeding handled by the examiner assigned the reexamination). When assigned to an assistant examiner due to lack of knowledgeable primary examiner, the SPE must sign and take responsibility for actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedies for inadvertent assignment to original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner' contrary to policy, concerned parties must timely alert the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patent owner or third party requester who objects must file a paper alerting the Office within two months of the first Office action or other Office communication indicating the examiner assignment; otherwise reassignment will not be considered. Reassignment is addressed case-by-case and assignment to the original examiner alone is not grounds to vacate prior Office decisions or to restart the reexamination. If a paper directed to examiner assignment has no right of entry (e.g., third party learns of assignment but has no right to file under the rules), the Office may waive rules to the extent necessary to enter and consider the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer procedure for reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure to request transfer of a reexamination proceeding from the art unit originally assigned to another art unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the SPE believes the reexamination should be assigned to another art unit, the SPE must obtain consent of the SPE of the desired art unit. Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 305, reexaminations must be conducted with special dispatch and transfers must be handled expeditiously: email the transfer request to the new SPE with cc to the SPREs of the TCs involved and to OPLA CRU; hand-carry any paper patent file to the new SPE; unresolved conflicts are to be resolved by the involved TC Directors. If new art unit accepts assignment, new SPE assigns to examiner and new TC's reexamination clerk PALMs in the request; SPREs of involved TCs and CRU must be notified of transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time reporting for reexamination activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All clerical and professional time expended on reexamination activities must be reported using specified PMS, Project, and payroll codes for accurate fee/cost recovery and workload accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical time: report using appropriate PMS Code and Project Code (include supervision, copying, typing, docketing). Professional time: directors, SPEs, examiners and Board members report on Time and Attendance Report using Project Codes: 119051 — activities related to a specific reexamination proceeding up until ex parte prosecution begins; 119052 — activities from first ex parte action until issuance of a certificate; 112084 — SPE review and training of examiners in reexamination. TC SPREs and paralegals use 1407-30 on Biweekly Time Worksheets. Time reported under 119051/119052 is also recorded in Examiner Production System as 'Other' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director-initiated reexamination authority and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may, at any time during the enforceability of a patent, determine whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised and may initiate ex parte reexamination without a request or fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally public requests asking the Director to undertake reexamination will not be considered. Employee-initiated cases: an Office employee aware of an unusual fact situation should forward a memorandum (including proposed rejections and supporting patents/printed publications) and the patent file through the TC supervisory chain to OPLA; include an electronic disk and paper copy. If ordered, OPLA prepares and signs the decision (Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy) and CRU mails it. CRU preprocessing prepares the reexamination file and Official Gazette notice, then forwards to the appropriate TC for examination and prosecution to proceed (contacting only the patent owner thereafter). If the Deputy Commissioner refuses to issue an order, no record is placed in the patent file and the patent owner is not notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for deciding a reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director (or examiner under delegated authority) must determine whether to order reexamination within three months following the filing date of the request (35 U.S.C. 303(a); 37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical timing guidance: examiner should take up the request for decision about 6 weeks after filing; the decision should be mailed within 10 weeks of the filing date. If the 3-month period ends on a weekend or Federal holiday in D.C., the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day. When reexamination for the same patent has already been ordered and is pending, the examiner should immediately take up the new request (no 6-week delay).

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation search and handling of litigation-involved patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination on a request, the examiner must request a litigation computer search by the Scientific and Technical Information Center (STIC) to check if the patent has been or is involved in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete the 'Litigation Review' box on the reexamination IFW file jacket form to indicate the review and results; scan the STIC search and file jacket form into the IFW reexamination file history. If record or STIC search indicates additional information desirable, seek guidance from the Office of the Solicitor for further litigation searching. If the patent is or was involved in litigation and a paper referring to court proceeding has been filed, reference that paper by number in the 'Litigation Review' box. If litigation is concluded or ongoing, promptly bring the request to the attention of the TC SPRE, who should review the decision and any examiner action to ensure conformity with Office litigation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and content of the examiner's determination on the request
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's determination whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised is based on the claims in effect at the time of determination; the determination becomes part of the official file and is mailed to the patent owner and requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments will not be considered when deciding requests if they: (1) were presented with the request by the patent owner, (2) were filed in a pending reexamination where the certificate has not been issued, or (3) were submitted in a reissue application on which no reissue patent has been issued. The decision's object is to grant or deny an order for reexamination (not to make a final determination of unpatentability). The decision should discuss ALL patent claims to inform the patent owner so a response may be made; the examiner should indicate initial positions on issues identified in the request to allow comment by the patent owner and requester. The examiner should limit discussion to whether a substantial new question has been raised and should not reject claims in the order for ex parte reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and threshold for 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination is ordered if the prior art patents and printed publications cited raise a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim of the patent; the term is developed case-by-case with case law guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art patents and printed publications raise a SNQ as to at least one claim, then SNQ is present unless the same question of patentability has already been decided by (A) a final holding of invalidity after all appeals, or (B) by the Office in a previous examination or pending reexamination of the patent. Only one claim need present a SNQ to order reexamination. No prima facie case of unpatentability need be found to grant an order for reexamination. A denial may be petitioned to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 within one month of mailing of the examiner's determination refusing reexamination; denial is final and nonappealable if no timely petition or if petition decision affirms refusal; partial refund of fee may be made when no SNQ is found (37 CFR 1.26(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests filed after reissue of the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after a reissue patent for that patent has issued, reexamination will be denied because the original patent has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reexamine a reissued patent, a new request must be filed based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent. If a reissue patent issues after the filing of a request for reexamination (see merge rules in MPEP § 2285).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for deciding second or subsequent requests during a pending reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a second or subsequent ex parte reexamination request is filed while a first ex parte reexamination is pending, whether to order depends on the prior art cited by the later requester and whether it raises a substantial new question of patentability different from that raised in the pending proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the later requester includes prior art that raised the SNQ in the pending reexamination, the second/subsequent request should be denied. If the later request raises a different SNQ or addresses new/amended claims proposed under 37 CFR 1.530(d) in the pending proceeding, reexamination may be ordered to permit examination of the entire patent package. The second/subsequent request should be determined on its own merits. In aggravated situations where the second/subsequent request appears filed for harassment (and a petition is granted), prosecution on the second/subsequent reexamination may be suspended. Merger of a second/subsequent request with an already pending proceeding that would unduly prolong conclusion is disfavored due to the requirement of special dispatch.
